messages.author: 4364ce565c0e42d1
messages.subject: Error: Failed to create the shared library.
parts:
Hey all, 
My question has to do with, how to explicitly include the path to some headers when nimble tries to compile our model.

Cmodel <<- compileNimble(model_pred, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)
compiling... this may take a minute. On some systems there may be some compiler warnings that can be safely ignored.
g++ -std=gnu++11 -I"/share/pkg.7/r/3.5.1/install/lib64/R/include" -DNDEBUG -DR_NO_REMAP   -DEIGEN_MPL2_ONLY=1 -I"/usr2/postdoc/hamzed/R/library/nimble/include" -Wno-misleading-indentation -Wno-ignored-attributes -Wno-deprecated-declarations  -I/usr/local/include   -fpic  -g -O2 -c dynamicRegistrations_03_06_09_54_24.cpp -o dynamicRegistrations_03_06_09_54_24.o
cc1plus: error: /project/earth/packages/hdf5-1.6.10/include: Permission denied
make: *** [dynamicRegistrations_03_06_09_54_24.o] Error 1
Error: Failed to create the shared library.

Here is the error I get from nimble where it looks for the hdf5 headers in a path that has changed. I was wondering if there is some way I can tell nimble to look into a specific path for HDF5 when compiling my model ?

messages.subject: Re: Error: Failed to create the shared library.
parts:
nimbleExternalCall?

well... no I was actually just trying to run simple model like this :

library(nimble)

code = nimbleCode({
  for(i in 1:5)
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu, sd = sigma)
  mu ~ dnorm(mu0,1)
  sigma ~ dunif(0,1)
  mu0 ~ dnorm(0,1)
  tmp[1:2] ~ dmnorm(tmp0[1:2], C[1:2,1:2])
  tmp0[1:2] ~ dmnorm(zeroes[1:2], C[1:2,1:2])
})

m = nimbleModel(code, data = list(y=rnorm(5)), inits = list(mu=1, mu0=0, sigma=.5, tmp0 = c(3,4), tmp = c(10,11)),
                constants = list(zeroes=rep(1,2), C = diag(2)))


cm = compileNimble(m, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Error: Failed to create the shared library.
parts: Oh, I see.  I thought it came from something specific you were doing with nimble.  Instead it must be something generic your compiler wants to use?  The error message doesn't seem to be that it can't find it but rather that permissions don't grant you access to it.  Do you specifically know of a change in your system's configuration? Have you installed any parts of your system recently, like an update to XCode on OS X, which may need you to launch it once outside of R to give it permissions?  Can you see the files in the given location and look at their permissions?  Otherwise this is fairly hard for us to help with.  It looks like it has to do with your configuration, not nimble per se, as far as I can see right now.
